title: Cross-region graded-degradation cascade: postmortem, runbook updates, and hardening plan
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: During a capacity transient in us-west we observed a cascade of graded-degradation decisions that caused simultaneous circuit-breaker closures in secondary regions, amplified backpressure, and a sustained SLO drift for 37 minutes. This ticket documents the timeline, root causes, contributing factors, and an actionable hardening plan including runbook/alert changes and follow-up engineering work.
impact_summary: Duration: ~37 minutes (2026-03-09 14:12–14:49 UTC). Affected services: text-generation API (gen.v1) and chat endpoints; ~18% of customer requests experienced p95 latency > 3s and several high-throughput customers saw transient error rates up to 6%. External-facing SLO (p95 latency < 400ms) was breached for 37 minutes causing degraded user experience for customer cohort on Dedicated and Hosted plans.
timeline:
2026-03-09 14:10 UTC: Rapid traffic spike in us-west observed on internal dashboard (traffic +2.6x baseline).
2026-03-09 14:12 UTC: Headroom in primary US region exhausted; smart-routing began failover to secondary regions (eu-west and ap-south) per policy.
2026-03-09 14:13–14:18 UTC: Secondary-region nodes received bursted fan-out; autoscaling attempted to satisfy throughput but instance spin-up lagged.
2026-03-09 14:18 UTC: Local circuit-breaker thresholds on eu-west tripped around the same time due to conservative hysteresis; control-plane rolled out graded-degradation measures (reduced token budgets and aggressive shedding).
2026-03-09 14:20 UTC: Multiple regions applied similar shedding simultaneously; priority queue starvation occurred for medium-priority requests leading to queue head-of-line blocking and KV-cache cold misses.
2026-03-09 14:25 UTC: Observability shows queue lengths and retry storms; error budget alarms fired but alert thresholds were missed by on-call routing rules for cascading failures.
2026-03-09 14:32 UTC: Emergency mitigation (manual lowering of circuit thresholds in eu-west, temporary routing to warm standby region) enacted by infra on-call.
2026-03-09 14:49 UTC: Traffic normalized and automated recovery resumed; gradual restoration to standard routing by 15:10 UTC.
Postmortem analysis window: 2026-03-10 to 2026-03-14.
root_cause: Primary cause was synchronous, overly-conservative circuit-breaker hysteresis and identical shedding policies applied across regions without accounting for warm-up state and autoscale lag. This created a positive feedback loop: failover -> burst -> CB trips -> more failover -> queue amplification. Additionally, KV cache cold starts amplified latency for failover traffic and our detection thresholds didn't escalate to 'cascade' mode quickly enough.
contributing_factors: Identical CB hysteresis and shedding thresholds in all regions (no differential for warm vs warmed regions)
Routing policy lacks staggered failover or jitter to avoid synchronized load jumps
Autoscaler warm-up time underestimated for the model instance type; scaling actions returned capacity too slowly
Priority queue algorithm allowed medium-priority traffic to preempt headrooms, causing starvation for critical requests
KV cache eviction policy results in cold-start latency spikes during mass failover
Alerting thresholds were tuned for single-region incidents and did not provide an early 'multi-region cascade' pager path
detection_and_response: Detection: Control-plane metrics (queue depth and p95 latency) showed degradation but multi-region cascade signature (simultaneous CB closures) was not instrumented. Response: On-call infra manually adjusted routing weights and lowered CB sensitivity in secondary regions, and enabled a warm-standby routing override. Time to initial mitigation: ~20 minutes. Time to full recovery: ~37 minutes. Post-incident we performed traffic replay tests to reproduce the failure mode in staging.
short_term_mitigation: Introduce temporary guardrail: increase stagger window for automated failover by 30s to prevent immediate synchronized fan-out (Config change rolled 2026-03-11)
Lower circuit-breaker sensitivity for warmed regions to prevent premature tripping (hotfix applied 2026-03-12)
Enable KV-prefetch on failover path to reduce cold-start hits (feature flag enabled 2026-03-12)
Add an emergency runbook step to enable warm-standby routing and manual weight adjustments (runbook patch PR #1289)
Add immediate alerting rule for 'simultaneous-CB-trip' pattern to page SREs (alert rule added 2026-03-13)
Whitelisting of high-priority customer flows from medium-priority shedding during cascade events (policy change 2026-03-13)
long_term_mitigations: Implement region-aware CB profiles: separate hysteresis and backoff for warm vs cold regions (design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/resilience/cb-profiles)
Upgrade autoscaler predictive model to include traffic burst forecasts and instance warm-up windows (timeline: Q2 2026)
Introduce probabilistic failover jitter and staged fan-out to reduce simultaneous capacity shifts (design/RFC created)
Rework priority-queue algorithm to enforce SLA qps guarantees and prevent head-of-line blocking under failover load
KV cache pre-warming strategies for failover traffic plus adaptive eviction tuned by failover likelihood
Formalize a 'multi-region cascade' alerting and on-call playbook with dedicated escalation path

playbook_changes: Add explicit step for detecting multi-region synchronized CB trips with metric queries and thresholds
Add 'stabilize before widen' decision: delay widening failover fan-out until KV cache warm-signal or warm-count threshold met
Checklist item: verify warm-standby routing path is healthy before redirecting >25% traffic
New emergency command: 'cb-relax-region <region> <minutes>' to temporarily increase CB thresholds
monitoring_and_alerting_changes: New metric: regions_with_active_cb_trips (count) and alert if >1 for >30s
New SLO-progress dashboard with per-region deviation and automatic correlation links to CB state
Pager path: multi-region-cascade -> page SRE lead, runtime on-call, and product incidents channel
Logged event enrichment: include routing weights, CB state, and KV-cache-hit-rate in all related alerts
